mainTopic: Who wrote the משנה about the unidentified stranger, the vows about a כּוֹי, and the start of the new פרק on the three things forbidden to a נזיר.
overview: The amud opens by asking who wrote the משנה about six people who vowed נזירות on the identity of an approaching stranger. That משנה says no one is a נזיר if the stranger turned back unidentified. The גמרא rejects רבי טרפון as the author, because he holds that such a vow never takes effect at all. It names רבי יהודה instead, who is lenient when a grain heap is lost and its size can never be checked. רבי שמעון is strict in both cases. A new משנה then describes people making opposite נזירות vows about whether a כּוֹי is a חיה or a בהמה, and it rules that all of them are נזירים. The גמרא compares two ברייתות, one counting nine נזירים and one counting nine terms of נזירות. רב ששת explains how a single person can carry nine terms. The פרק בית שמאי then ends, and a new פרק opens with the three things forbidden to a נזיר: טומאה, shaving, and grapevine products.

steps.title: Can the author be רבי טרפון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה follows רבי טרפון, then questions whether רבי טרפון would ever make him a נזיר at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the משנה follows רבי טרפון, that doesn't work. Would רבי טרפון ever make him a נזיר? When he made the vow, he did not know whether the stranger was so-and-so, so how could נזירות take effect on him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests whether רבי טרפון could be the author of the משנה. It points out a problem right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה implies that if the stranger had been identified, someone would be a נזיר. But רבי טרפון looks at the moment of the vow, and at that moment the person did not know who the stranger was. So for רבי טרפון the vow never takes effect, even if the stranger is identified later.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (offering a possible answer, usually about to be rejected)

phrases.english: If you say it is Rabbi Tarfon —
is he a nazir at all?
Since at the time that he vowed

phrases.aramaic: לָא יָדַע אִי פְּלוֹנִי הוּא וְאִי לָא,
phrases.english: he did not know whether it was so-and-so or not,
does nezirus take effect on him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier question of who the author of the משנה is.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי טרפון is the author of the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה implies there would be a נזיר if the stranger were identified. But for רבי טרפון, a vow made without knowing the facts never takes effect at all.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי טרפון's view
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי טרפון: none of them is a נזיר, because נזירות needs a clearly stated vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says in the name of רבי טרפון that not one of them is a נזיר, because נזירות only takes effect when the vow is stated clearly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up its challenge. It proves that רבי טרפון says no one is a נזיר in this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון requires הפלאה, a vow that is clear at the moment it is said. A vow that depends on an unknown fact is not clear, so it fails from the start. That is why רבי טרפון cannot be the author of a משנה that only frees them when the stranger stays unidentified.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught (in a ברייתא), introducing a source that contradicts
A clear, explicit statement of a vow

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up רבי טרפון's principle: a vow that is unclear when it is made does not take effect.

phrases.english: But it was taught in a baraisa,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehudah says in the name of Rabbi Tarfon:
not one of them is a nazir,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the six people in the earlier משנה who each vowed about the stranger.

phrases.english: because nezirus was not given
except for a clearly stated vow!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to prove the challenge in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי טרפון holds no one is a נזיר, even if the stranger is identified.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי יהודה in the name of רבי טרפון, based on הפלאה.

steps.title: The author is רבי יהודה of the grain heap
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי יהודה's view in the case of the grain heap.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the משנה follows רבי יהודה, the one who ruled about the grain heap.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops רבי טרפון and gives a new answer: רבי יהודה. It is about to bring the source for this answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה agrees that a vow tied to an unknown fact can take effect. But when the fact can never be checked, he rules leniently. That fits the משנה exactly: if the stranger turned back unidentified, no one is a נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: A heap or pile of grain

phrases.english: Rather, it is Rabbi Yehudah of the grain heap.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected suggestion of רבי טרפון.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Names a different author for the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה might have followed רבי טרפון.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי יהודה, who is lenient when the fact can never be checked.

steps.title: The case of the stolen grain heap
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: someone vowed to be a נזיר if a heap held 100 כור, and the heap was stolen or lost. רבי שמעון is strict and רבי יהודה is lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: someone said, "I am a נזיר on condition that this heap contains a hundred כור." Then he went and found that it had been stolen or lost. רבי שמעון forbids him, treating him as a נזיר, and רבי יהודה permits him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that shows רבי יהודה's lenient view, which is the source for the answer in step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heap can no longer be measured, so we will never know whether the condition was met. רבי יהודה says that in such a doubt he is not a נזיר. This is the same as the stranger who left without being identified.

phrases.english: As it was taught:
"I am hereby a nazir

phrases.aramaic: עַל מְנָת שֶׁיְּהֵא בַּכְּרִי הַזֶּה מֵאָה כּוֹר״,
phrases.english: on condition that this heap contains a hundred kor,"
and he went and found it
that it had been stolen or lost —
Rabbi Shimon forbids,
phrases.notes: He forbids wine and the like, meaning he treats the man as a נזיר.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehudah permits.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר עַל מְנָת שֶׁיְּהֵא בַּכְּרִי הַזֶּה מֵאָה כּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for naming רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה is lenient when the condition can never be checked.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the stolen or lost grain heap.

steps.title: Why רבי שמעון is strict in both cases
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון reasons that since he would have been a נזיר if the facts were known, he is a נזיר now too. The same applies to the unidentified stranger.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון holds: if the heap had not been stolen, maybe it would have held 100 כור and he would be a נזיר, so now too he is a נזיר. Here too: if the stranger had come to us and we knew he was so-and-so, the man would be a נזיר, so now too he is a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי שמעון's strict view. It shows that he would disagree with our משנה in the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, losing the evidence does not remove the doubt. Since he might be a נזיר, he must act as one. This confirms that the משנה, which says no one is a נזיר, follows רבי יהודה and not רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: And here too (applying the same logic to our case)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה (no one is a נזיר if the stranger was never identified) follows רבי יהודה, who is lenient when the fact can never be checked. רבי טרפון says the vow never takes effect at all. רבי שמעון says he remains a נזיר because of the doubt.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon holds:
since if it had not been stolen,
perhaps it would have had a hundred kor in it
and he would be a nazir —
now too he is a nazir.
And here too,
since if he had come before us
and we knew that he was so-and-so,
he would be a nazir —
now too he is a nazir.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר כֵּיוָן דְּאִילּוּ לֹא נִגְנַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the opposing view in the ברייתא and applies it to our משנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי שמעון treats an unresolvable doubt strictly, so the lenient משנה must follow רבי יהודה.

steps.title: New משנה: vows about a כּוֹי
steps.stepSummary: People see a כּוֹי and make opposite נזירות vows on whether it is a חיה or a בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: someone saw a כּוֹי and said, "I am a נזיר if this is a חיה." Others said: "I am a נזיר if this is not a חיה," "I am a נזיר if this is a בהמה," and "I am a נזיר if this is not a בהמה."
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets up a case of several vows that all depend on the status of the כּוֹי, an animal whose category is in doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כּוֹי has signs of both a חיה and a בהמה, so no one can say for sure which vow came true. This is a new kind of doubt: the question can never be settled, not because the evidence was lost but because the animal itself is uncertain. The ruling on these vows comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal whose status between חיה and בהמה is uncertain

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה can be read as several people each making one vow, or as one person making several vows. In steps 9 and 10 the גמרא discusses both readings, including one man making all six vows about the animal.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
He saw a koy and said:
"I am hereby a nazir if this is a wild animal,"
"I am hereby a nazir if this is not a wild animal,"
"I am hereby a nazir if this is a domesticated animal,"
"I am hereby a nazir if this is not a domesticated animal."

steps.triggerLanguage: רָאָה אֶת הַכּוֹי וְאָמַר הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר שֶׁזֶּה חַיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה about another kind of doubtful נזירות vow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case of opposite נזירות vows about whether a כּוֹי is a חיה or a בהמה. The ruling follows later.

steps.title: The rest of the vows, and everyone becomes a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes the list of vows about the כּוֹי, adds three vows about the other people, and rules that all of them are נזירים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another says: 'I am a נזיר if this is both a wild animal and a farm animal.' Another: 'I am a נזיר if this is neither a wild animal nor a farm animal.' Another: 'I am a נזיר if one of you is a נזיר.' Another: 'I am a נזיר if none of you is a נזיר.' Another: 'I am a נזיר if all of you are נזירים.' The ruling: they are all נזירים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list of opposite vows about the כּוֹי and then rules that every single person who vowed is a נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two vows here are about the animal itself: it is both kinds, or it is neither kind. The last three vows are about the group of people who already vowed. Even though the vows contradict each other, the משנה makes everyone a נזיר, because the כּוֹי really is a doubtful creature.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I am hereby a נזיר,' the standard opening words of the vow

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think that only one side can 'win' here. With a כּוֹי, the משנה makes every vow-maker a נזיר, even though the vows contradict each other.

phrases.english: 'I am hereby a nazir if this is a wild animal and a domestic animal,'

phrases.aramaic: ״הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר שֶׁאֵין זֶה לֹא חַיָּה וְלֹא בְּהֵמָה״,
phrases.english: 'I am hereby a nazir if this is neither a wild animal nor a domestic animal,'
'I am hereby a nazir if one of you is a nazir,'
'I am hereby a nazir if not one of you is a nazir,'
'I am hereby a nazir if all of you are nazirs' —
they are all nazirs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the list of vows about the כּוֹי that began in step 6, and gives the final ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone who made one of these vows about the כּוֹי, or about the group, is a נזיר.

steps.title: Two teachings: nine נזירים or nine נזירויות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes two ברייתות. One counts the case as nine people who are נזירים, and the other counts it as nine terms of נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: One ברייתא teaches: nine נזירים. Another ברייתא teaches: nine נזירויות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up two different ways of counting the משנה's case. This prepares the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Nine נזירים' sounds like nine different people. 'Nine נזירויות' sounds like nine terms of נזירות, which could all fall on one person. The difference in wording is what the גמרא will now look into.

keyTerms.meaning: Terms of נזירות (in this ברייתא, nine terms)

phrases.english: GEMARA: One [baraita] teaches:
nine nazirs,
and the other [baraita] teaches: nine naziriteships.
phrases.notes: 'Naziriteships' means separate terms of being a נזיר, not separate people.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי חֲדָא תִּשְׁעָה נְזִירִים וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ תֵּשַׁע נְזִירִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's discussion of the משנה's ruling that 'they are all נזירים.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two ways of counting the case: nine people, or nine terms of נזירות.

steps.title: Nine people is clear, but how does one man get nine terms?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts 'nine נזירים' as nine different people. It then asks how nine terms of נזירות could ever fall on a single man.
steps.simpleTranslation: Nine נזירים makes sense: there were many men, and each one tied his vow to this animal. But nine נזירויות for one man, how can you find such a case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first ברייתא easily. It then challenges the second ברייתא: how could one person end up with nine terms?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The form 'בשלמא... אלא' means: 'the first is fine, but the second is a problem.' Nine different men each making one vow is simple. One man holding all nine terms is hard to picture.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It makes sense': this part is understandable
He tied his vow to it, linking his נזירות to this animal
How can you find such a case?

phrases.english: It makes sense [that there are] nine nazirs —
for example, where there were many men,
who kept tying [their vows] to it.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the כּוֹי; each man linked his own vow to what that animal is.

phrases.english: But nine naziriteships for one man —
how can you find it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא תֵּשַׁע נְזִירִיּוֹת לְחַד גַּבְרָא הֵיכִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the first ברייתא and challenges the second one.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא that counts nine נזירויות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nine terms seem to need nine separate vow-makers. So how could one man carry all nine?

steps.title: Six terms work, but the last three don't
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא narrows the problem. One person could say all six vows about the animal, but the three vows about 'you' cannot come from the same person.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that you can find six, as the משנה taught. But how can you find the other three?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens its question. Six terms on one person is possible, so the real problem is only the last three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The six vows about the כּוֹי (wild, not wild, farm animal, not farm animal, both, neither) can all be said by one man. The last three vows talk about the other people ('one of you,' 'none of you,' 'all of you'). That means someone outside the group has to say them.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in the משנה

phrases.english: It makes sense that you find six, as we learned [in the mishnah].
But the three, how can you find them!
phrases.notes: The three are the vows about 'you': one of you, none of you, all of you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the challenge from step 9 down to the last three terms.
steps.kashyaTarget: The last three terms in the count of nine נזירויות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The last three vows refer to the other vow-makers, so one man cannot be both a speaker in the group and the person talking about the group.

steps.title: רב ששת: taking on everyone's נזירות
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that a person can say 'I am a נזיר, and the נזירות of all of them is on me,' and so take on all nine terms.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: For example, where someone said, 'I am a נזיר, and the נזירות of all of them is upon me.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question by describing how one person can end up with nine terms.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nine people made the nine vows in the משנה, and each of them is a נזיר. A tenth person then accepts every one of their terms on himself, so he now carries nine terms of נזירות.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who gives the answer
'The נזירות of all of them is upon me'

steps.whatToRemember: Nine נזירים means nine people, one vow each. Nine נזירויות means one person who accepts all nine of their terms, as רב ששת explains.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
For example, where he said:
'I am hereby a nazir, and the naziriteship of all [of them] is upon me.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in steps 9 and 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a specific case (אוקימתא) that makes the count work
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One man could not have nine terms, because the last three vows need outside speakers.
steps.terutzMaskana: A man who takes on the נזירות of all nine vow-makers carries nine terms.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: The formula הדרן עלך marks the end of the פרק called בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק בית שמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is not part of the argument. It is a closing formula that marks the end of the פרק we have been learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פרק is named by its opening words, and this one began with בית שמאי. Saying הדרן shows love for the learning and the hope of coming back to review it. After this line, a brand-new topic begins.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. This is the formula said when finishing a פרק.
The name of the פרק that is ending, taken from its opening words.

steps.whatToRemember: The discussion of the nine terms of נזירות is finished. A new פרק, with a new subject, starts right after this line.

phrases.english: We will return to you, [the chapter] בית שמאי
phrases.notes: This is the traditional goodbye to a chapter, and the chapter is named by its first words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally closes the פרק whose final sugya ended with רב ששת's answer in step 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק בית שמאי is complete.

steps.title: The three things forbidden to a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה lists three kinds of things forbidden to a נזיר: טומאה, shaving, and grapevine products. Grapevine products combine with each other, and liability starts at a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three kinds of things are forbidden to a נזיר: becoming טמא, shaving his hair, and anything that comes from the grapevine. All the different grapevine products join together to make up the amount. He is not liable until he eats a כזית from the grapes.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק opens with a משנה that lays out the basic list of what a נזיר may not do. It then gives two rules about the grapevine prohibition: the products combine, and the minimum amount is a כזית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה sorts the נזיר's prohibitions into three groups. The group 'what comes from the vine' covers many different foods, so the משנה tells us that small amounts of different vine products count together toward the minimum. It also sets the amount that makes him liable at a כזית.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who has taken a vow of נזירות.
Ritual impurity. For a נזיר, this means becoming impure from a dead body.
Anything that comes from the grapevine, such as wine, grapes, or raisins.
They combine. Different items join together to make up the required amount.
The size of an olive, a standard minimum amount for eating.

steps.confusionAlert: 'Combine' does not mean that each product needs its own כזית. A little of one vine product plus a little of another can add up together to one כזית.
steps.whyThisMatters: This three-part list is the basic map of נזירות, and the rest of the פרק builds on it.

phrases.english: Three types [of things] are forbidden to a nazir:
impurity, and shaving,
and whatever comes out of the grapevine.
And everything that comes out of the grapevine
combines, one with the other.
phrases.notes: Different vine products count together toward the minimum amount.

phrases.english: And he is not liable until he eats
an olive-bulk of the grapes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק after the הדרן, introducing a new subject unrelated to the previous sugya.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נזיר is forbidden three things: טומאה, shaving, and grapevine products. All vine products combine, and liability begins at a כזית.
